transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well... I suppose what brought me in is that I had a bit of an outburst the other day. I blew up at one of the younger volunteers over a crooked tablecloth of all things. Just lost my temper completely. And... well, I don't usually talk to people that way. It bothered me enough that I figured I should come in and talk to someone about it.
Has this kind of irritability or short temper been happening only recently, or have you noticed it building up over weeks or months?
No, it hasn't been building up for months. It's really just been recently. I'd say this has been going on for about a week now... ever since the robbery outside the bank.
Since the robbery, have you been having any unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about the event?

Yes, I have. Not nightmares, really, but... the memories, yes. Out of nowhere, I'll just hear that man's rough voice in my head. Or I'll see the donation envelope hitting the ground again. It happens even when I'm just sitting quietly at my kitchen table. It just pops into my mind without any warning.
Since the robbery, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, situations, or things that remind you of that day?

Yes, I have. I've actually been taking the long way around when I go out, just so I don't have to pass by the bank. And... well, I haven't gone into the festival storage room either. Going in there just brings the whole thing a bit too close, so I've been staying away from it.
Can you tell me exactly how many days ago the robbery happened?
Well, like I said earlier, it's been about a week now. The robbery happened exactly a week ago.
Since the robbery, have you felt strangely detached from yourself or your surroundings, like you're in a daze or watching things happen from outside your body?

No, I haven't felt anything like that. I mean, I'm fully here. I feel like myself, just... maybe a little more on edge than usual. But no, I haven't been walking around in a daze or feeling like I'm watching things from the outside. I always know exactly where I am.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient experienced a clearly defined traumatic event (witnessing an armed robbery) one week prior to presentation. She reports intrusive re-experiencing (unbidden memories of the assailant's voice and the envelope hitting the ground), avoidance of trauma-related cues (avoiding the bank route and the storage room), and increased arousal/irritability (the outburst over the tablecloth, feeling 'on edge'). She denies dissociative symptoms such as depersonalization or derealization. Because the trauma occurred only one week ago and symptoms have been present for less than one month, the diagnosis of PTSD (F43.1) cannot yet be made, as it requires symptom duration exceeding one month. The temporal proximity to a severe, life-threatening stressor along with intrusion, avoidance, and hyperarousal symptoms best fits Acute Stress Reaction (F43.0). Adjustment disorder (F43.2) is less likely given the severity and specific trauma-related intrusive/avoidant symptomatology, which points to a more acute stress response rather than a general maladaptive reaction to stress.
